Windows Build, Packaging, Release, and Final Build Plan

purpose: Produce a reproducible Windows 11 portable build with predictable native dependencies, verification, checksums, and rollback.
evidence: Current release already uses PyInstaller onedir + ZIP and verifies root executable/tool slot structure.
Potential V2 native media libraries can significantly change DLL/runtime packaging complexity.
decisions: Keep portable onedir ZIP as the first V2 distribution target unless a later approved release decision adds an installer.
Do not bundle optional native libraries until license and redistribution obligations are documented.
Release artifacts must be generated by CI from an exact commit and verified before publication.
V2 must retain an easily reversible reference build path using the proven FFmpeg backend.
tasks: Define pinned Python, PySide6, PyInstaller, and all optional native library versions for release candidate.
Build dependency manifest and third-party notices/license bundle.
Create portable verification: executable, required DLLs/plugins, tool discovery, fresh-machine smoke, no developer absolute paths, writable user-data locations.
Run Windows 11 x64 clean-environment tests, common DPI settings, paths with spaces/Unicode, and machines without system FFmpeg if app-local tool policy requires external setup.
Generate BUILD_INFO, SHA256SUMS, source archive, release notes, migration notes, and known limitations.
Define release candidate -> user test -> final release promotion with immutable tag and overwrite guards.
gate: PASS when clean Windows portable smoke succeeds without developer environment assumptions.
PASS when license/notice obligations match bundled binaries.
PASS when artifact checksum and source commit are recorded.
PASS when rollback to previous stable build is documented and tested.

Implementation Sequence, Gates, Rollback, and AI Handoff

purpose: Convert all approved planning into a safe implementation order so another AI can continue without re-planning, skipping gates, or editing the wrong repository.
evidence: The project is intentionally planning-first; code changes are forbidden until planning/source-of-truth documents are complete and reviewed.
Original repository must remain untouched; implementation target is V2-AI-Video-Composer only.
decisions: Implementation proceeds in small waves with a green baseline after every wave.
No large-bang replacement of render, animation, timeline, and UI in one branch.
Every risky backend/dependency change uses a feature flag/adapter and has an exit path.
A later AI must read planning docs, current status, architecture rules, and latest gate before coding.
tasks: Wave A: documentation/source-of-truth commit and baseline CI re-run in V2 without functional changes.
Wave B: architecture interfaces/capability model with FFmpeg behavior unchanged.
Wave C: render validation/progress/cancellation hardening and benchmark harness.
Wave D: animation/keyframe data model and migration with current effects preserved.
Wave E: new motion/effect implementations in small capability groups with preview/final parity tests.
Wave F: timeline/manual-editing improvements and validation UX.
Wave H: optional mature-backend spike(s); promote only if measured acceptance criteria pass.
Wave I: UI polish after behavior is stable; screenshot regression update only with explicit approval.
Wave J: full regression, Windows packaging, user test build, final release candidate, final release.
At each wave: branch/commit, tests, evidence, gate PASS/FAIL, exact next action, rollback point.
gate: CODING GATE: all planning DOCX and planning index are present in V2 repo and reviewed.
DEPENDENCY GATE: mature component adoption has license + Windows packaging evidence.
UI GATE: UI reference changes are approved before implementation.
RELEASE GATE: full regression + clean Windows portable + user acceptance evidence pass.
HANDOFF GATE: next AI can state current wave, completed work, unresolved risks, and next exact action from repository docs alone.
risks: Skipping planning after a successful spike
